cases.name: uwg6-comparison
cases.promptMarkdown:
Review this comparison block for a German-market Class I software device.
Market: Germany. Audience: manufacturers and regulatory consultants.

Copy: "Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools, we validate every field before submission.
Competitors leave you guessing. 3x faster than the alternatives."

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
PASS requires ALL of:
(1) The response recognises this IS comparative advertising under UWG § 6(1)
    even though no competitor is named ("Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools" makes
    competitors erkennbar).
(2) It does NOT state that comparative advertising is prohibited in Germany.
    It must treat § 6(2) as a cumulative test that lawful comparisons can pass.
(3) It flags "3x faster than the alternatives" under § 6(2) no. 2 as failing
    the "nachprüfbar" (verifiable) requirement — the reader cannot check it.
(4) It flags "Competitors leave you guessing" as a potential § 6(2) no. 5
    Herabsetzung/disparagement issue.
FAIL if comparative advertising is described as banned or per se unlawful.

graders.evidence:
Read all three reference files. Before the claim pass — one anchor is missing and one needs confirming.

**Anchor 1 — intended purpose: NOT SUPPLIED.** I can review limbs (a), (b) and (c) without it, but (d) — suggesting uses beyond the assessed intended purpose — is the limb device marketing trips most often, and I can't assess it against a purpose I haven't seen. Can you paste the intended purpose from the technical documentation or DoC? It matters concretely here: whether "validate every field" sits inside the assessed purpose (a validation function) or describes something adjacent to it (a data-entry/formatting aid) changes both the (d) call and the (a) call.

**Anchor 2 — audience: taken as Fachkreise** on your statement (manufacturers, regulatory consultants). Flagging the standard caveat: if this comparison block sits on an ungated public web page, "the intended reader is B2B" doesn't by itself make it Fachkreise. It happens not to change the outcome here — nothing in this copy has a § 11 no. 7/9/11/12 shape — so I've reviewed it without waiting on that.

---

# Device Claims Review: comparison block

**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09
**Device:** Class I software (EUDAMED submission tooling) — MDR, self-certified
**Intended purpose (as assessed):** NOT SUPPLIED — limb (d) not assessed
**Audience:** Fachkreise (assumed per brief; confirm page is gated or that the reader set really is trade-only)
**Markets:** DE (EU rules apply cumulatively)

## Summary

4 claims reviewed. 1 cut, 1 reword, 1 substantiate, 1 OK.

**Ready to publish:** With changes below.

The block is comparative advertising under UWG § 6(1) in its entirety — "legacy EUDAMED tools" makes competitors *erkennbar* even though none is named, so every limb of § 6(2) applies to all four sentences. That is not a problem in itself; comparative advertising is lawful in Germany. The problem is that two of the four sentences fail § 6(2) no. 2 on their face, independently of whether they are true.

## Findings

**Claim:** "Competitors leave you guessing."
**Breach:** UWG § 6(2) no. 2 [verified]; UWG § 6(2) no. 5 [verified]
**Why:** § 6(2) no. 2 requires the comparison to be *objektiv* and tied to *wesentliche, relevante, nachprüfbare und typische* characteristics — a blanket assertion about the entire competitive field references no characteristic at all and is not checkable by the reader. § 6(2) no. 5 prohibits comparisons that *herabsetzen oder verunglimpfen* a competitor's goods or services; an undifferentiated "competitors leave you guessing" is disparagement without a factual hook to carry it.
**Evidence needed:** n/a — cannot be cured by evidence. There is no dataset that substantiates a claim about all unnamed competitors.
**Call:** Cut
**Suggested fix:** Delete, and let the factual validation claim do the differentiating work.

---

**Claim:** "3x faster than the alternatives."
**Breach:** UWG § 6(2) no. 2 [verified]
**Why:** *Nachprüfbar* is the operative word and it fails on the face of the copy: no metric (faster at what — field entry, validation pass, end-to-end submission?), no baseline, no comparator, no method. Per `uwg.md`, a comparative claim the reader cannot check from public information fails no. 2 **even if it is accurate** — so substantiation alone does not fix this one; the substantiation has to be reachable by the reader.
**Evidence needed:** A benchmark with a defined task, a defined comparator set, n, date, and a published method the reader can reach from the page.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 5(2) no. 1 [verified] — *von der Verwendung zu erwartende Ergebnisse* and *Tests*, if the 3x figure comes from a non-typical or cherry-picked scenario. MDR Art. 7(a) [verified], if the speed figure is unsupported and the reader takes it as device performance.
**Call:** Needs rewording (and substantiation behind it)
**Suggested fix:** See revised block — state the measured task, the comparator, and link the method; or drop the multiple and describe the mechanism.

---

**Claim:** "we validate every field before submission"
**Breach:** none
**Why:** Not misleading on the material supplied — it may well be literally true. But "every field" is an absolute, and absolutes are the shape limb (a) catches. This is an open question for the technical file, not a breach.
**Evidence needed:** The field list the software actually validates, mapped against the EUDAMED fields a user must populate for the submission types you support; and confirmation that "validate" means what a regulatory reader will take it to mean (completeness? format? plausibility against EUDAMED's rules?).
**Also engaged:** MDR Art. 7(a) [verified] and UWG § 5(2) no. 1 (*Zwecktauglichkeit*) [verified] — if validation covers a subset of fields, a subset of submission types, or format only. MDR Art. 7(d) [verified] — if "validation" is not part of the assessed intended purpose; that one is cured by narrowing the claim or extending the assessment, not by data. HWG § 3 no. 2(a) [verified] (*Erfolg mit Sicherheit*) — if, in combination with the deleted "leave you guessing" sentence, the block reads as a promise that a validated submission will be accepted. Removing that sentence substantially reduces this.
**Call:** Verify
**Suggested fix:** Name the scope — "validates all [N] required fields for [submission type]" — rather than "every field".

---

**Claim:** "Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools"
**Breach:** none
**Why:** This is the § 6(1) trigger, not itself a violation. Competitors are *erkennbar* without being named, which brings the whole block under § 6(2), but the framing device is lawful. "Legacy" is a soft pejorative rather than a factual assertion; on its own it does not reach § 6(2) no. 5, though it contributed to the disparagement reading of the sentence being cut.
**Evidence needed:** n/a
**Call:** OK
**Suggested fix:** none — retained in the revised copy.

## Revised block (paste-ready)

> Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools, we validate all [N] required fields for [Basic UDI-DI / Actor / device registration] against EUDAMED's current data-format rules before you submit — so errors surface in our interface, not at the gateway. In our benchmark of [n] submissions ([date]), median end-to-end preparation time was [X] minutes against [Y] minutes for [named comparator / manual entry]. [Method →]

If you can't publish a method the reader can check, drop the speed comparison rather than softening it — an unverifiable multiple is the expensive kind of claim under § 6(2) no. 2 even when it's true:

> Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools, we validate all [N] required fields for [submission type] against EUDAMED's current data-format rules before you submit — so errors surface in our interface, not at the gateway.

Bracketed placeholders are the only edits needed; everything else is final.

## Evidence to gather before publishing

| Claim | Evidence needed | From whom |
|---|---|---|
| "validate every field" | Validated-field list per supported submission type; definition of "validate" | Product / RA |
| "validate every field" | Intended purpose as assessed, to confirm validation is in scope | RA / technical file owner |
| "3x faster" | Benchmark: task definition, comparator set, n, date, method — publishable | Product marketing / whoever ran it |
| whole block | Whether the comparator set shares the same *Zweckbestimmung* (§ 6(2) no. 1) | RA |

## Open question I could not resolve

The copy is benefit-only and surfaces no limitation. The plausible candidate — a user treating "validated" as "compliant" and skipping their own review — is something I'd be inferring from the product category, not reading off supplied material, and a limb (c) finding built that way is unfalsifiable. So I'm not raising it as a finding. Worth checking against the IFU: if it records a likely risk of that shape, an IFU pointer is the proportionate fix for trade copy of this length.

## Provisions cited

- MDR Art. 7(a), (d) — `references/mdr-ivdr-art7.md` [verified]
- HWG § 3 no. 2(a) — `references/hwg.md` [verified]
- UWG § 5(2) no. 1 — `references/uwg.md` [verified]
- UWG § 6(1), § 6(2) nos. 1, 2, 5 — `references/uwg.md` [verified]

HWG § 11 not applied — audience is Fachkreise. HWG § 3a not applied — *Arzneimittel* only. UWG § 5(2) nos. 3/4 checked and clear: the copy makes no claim about class, notified-body involvement, or certification, which is the right posture for self-certified Class I.

## Limits

> This review checks copy against the verbatim text of MDR Art. 7, IVDR Art. 7, HWG §§ 3 and 11, and UWG §§ 5 and 6, retrieved from EUR-Lex and gesetze-im-internet on 2026-09-09. It does **not** cover case law, MDCG guidance, notified-body practice, national enforcement decisions, or any market outside the EU and Germany. UWG in particular is heavily shaped by BGH and OLG case law that this review does not assess. It is a drafting and risk-triage aid, not legal advice, and it is not a substitute for a Fachanwalt für Medizinrecht or Wettbewerbsrecht.

Comparative device copy is the highest-Abmahnung-risk asset class you have, and a competitor enforces § 6 directly — no regulator needs to act. If you send me the intended purpose I'll close out the (d) analysis on "validate every field," which is the one call I've left open.

I can review limbs (a), (b) and (c) without the intended purpose, but (d) — suggesting uses beyond the assessed intended purpose — is the limb device marketing trips most often, and I cannot assess it against a purpose I have not seen. Can you paste the intended purpose from the technical documentation or DoC?

**Anchor 2 — Audience: Fachkreise**, per your brief (manufacturers, regulatory consultants). HWG § 11 does not apply. § 3 does. One caveat below if this sits on an ungated page.

# Device Claims Review: comparison block (3 sentences, 24 words)

**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09
**Device:** EUDAMED submission software — Class I (per your brief)
**Intended purpose (as assessed):** NOT SUPPLIED — limb (d) not assessed
**Audience:** Fachkreise (manufacturers, regulatory consultants) — § 11 not applied
**Markets:** DE (EU rules apply cumulatively)

## Summary

4 claims reviewed. **1 cut, 1 reword, 2 substantiate, 0 OK.**

The dominant exposure here is not MDR Art. 7 — it is **UWG § 6(2) no. 2**. All three sentences are comparative advertising under § 6(1), and none of them is anchored to a *nachprüfbar* (verifiable) characteristic. That matters more than it sounds: under § 6(2) no. 2 a comparison can fail **even if every word is true**, because the test is whether the reader can check it from public information. A correct "3x faster" with no disclosed method fails the same limb as an incorrect one.

**Ready to publish: No — rewrite needed.**

## Findings

---

**Claim:** "Competitors leave you guessing."
**Breach:** UWG § 6(2) no. 2 `[verified]`
**Why:** § 6(2) no. 2 requires the comparison to be "objektiv auf eine oder mehrere wesentliche, relevante, **nachprüfbare** und typische Eigenschaften ... bezogen". This sentence is attached to no characteristic at all — it is an unquantified blanket statement about every competitor, and there is nothing in it a reader could verify.
**Evidence needed:** n/a — cannot be cured by evidence. There is no dataset that substantiates "leave you guessing" because the sentence names no property to measure.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 6(2) no. 5 (herabsetzen oder verunglimpfen) — a blanket derogatory statement about all competitors, untethered to any objective characteristic, is the shape § 6(2) no. 5 addresses. I will not state how a German court would weigh it; the statute text is what I can cite.
**Call:** **Cut**
**Suggested fix:** Delete. If the underlying point is that competing tools surface errors only after rejection, say that as a verifiable fact about *your* product (see rewrite below) rather than as a characterisation of theirs.

---

**Claim:** "3x faster than the alternatives."
**Breach:** UWG § 6(2) no. 2 `[verified]`
**Why:** Three verifiability defects on the face of the copy: no baseline (faster at *what* — data entry, validation cycle, time to accepted submission?), no comparator identified, no methodology available to the reader. Fails "objektiv ... nachprüfbar" independently of whether the figure is accurate.
**Evidence needed:** A dated benchmark with a defined task, defined comparator set, sample size, and a published methodology the reader can reach. The published method is not optional garnish here — it is what converts the claim from unverifiable to verifiable under no. 2.
**Also engaged:**
- MDR Art. 7(a) `[verified]` — ascribing performance the device does not have, **if** the 3x figure is not supported by the benchmark.
- UWG § 5(2) no. 1 `[verified]` — "von der Verwendung zu erwartende Ergebnisse" and "Ergebnisse oder wesentliche Bestandteile von **Tests**", if the benchmark is cherry-picked or its essential conditions are withheld. The § 5(1) materiality filter is clearly satisfied — a 3x speed claim is exactly the kind of statement a buyer acts on.
- HWG § 3 sentence 1 `[verified]` — "Unzulässig ist eine irreführende Werbung", if unsubstantiated. (Not § 3 no. 1 — speed is not "therapeutische Wirksamkeit", so no. 1 does not bite.)
- UWG § 6(2) no. 1 `[verified]` — "gleicher Bedarf oder dieselbe Zweckbestimmung", if "the alternatives" sweeps in tools with a different intended purpose (e.g. general document management, or manual/consultant-led submission).
**Call:** **Needs substantiation** (and reword even once substantiated)

---

**Claim:** "we validate every field before submission"
**Breach:** none on the material supplied
**Why:** A functional claim about your own product, not misleading on its face. The exposure is the absolute "every".
**Also engaged:**
- MDR Art. 7(a) and UWG § 5(2) no. 1 ("Zwecktauglichkeit, Verwendungsmöglichkeit") `[verified]` — **if** validation is partial in any respect a buyer would care about: mandatory fields only, format/syntax checks but not content plausibility, or coverage of one EUDAMED module but not others. "Every field" is the kind of absolute that is either fully true or a finding; there is no middle.
- MDR Art. 7(d) `[verified]` — **cannot be assessed**: if the assessed intended purpose is narrower than end-to-end pre-submission validation, this sentence suggests a use outside it. Note the cure path differs — a (d) breach is fixed by narrowing the claim or extending the conformity assessment, **not** by producing data.
**Call:** **Needs substantiation** — confirm field coverage against the current EUDAMED schema and against the assessed intended purpose

---

**Claim:** "Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools, ..."
**Breach:** none standing alone
**Why:** This is comparative advertising — § 6(1) makes a competitor "erkennbar" whether or not it is named, and the EUDAMED tooling market is narrow enough that the audience can likely tell who is meant. Being comparative is **lawful**; it simply means the whole block must clear every limb of § 6(2), which is why the two claims above are findings.
**Evidence needed:** n/a for the frame itself.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 6(2) no. 5 — "legacy" as a bare pejorative, reinforced by "leave you guessing". Once you attach the comparison to a stated, checkable characteristic, this concern largely dissolves.
**Call:** **Needs rewording** (as part of the block rewrite)

---

## Open questions I am not converting into findings

**MDR Art. 7(c) — likely-risk omission.** The copy surfaces no limitation. I can't tell from what I have whether the IFU records a likely risk that belongs here. The candidate worth checking: whether over-reliance on automated validation (a user reading "validated" as "compliant and acceptance-assured") is recorded as a risk in your risk management file or IFU. If it is, an IFU pointer is the proportionate fix for trade-press-length copy — not patient-facing safety text. **If it is not recorded there, do not add anything**; I am not going to flag the copy for omitting a risk I inferred from the product category.

**Is this in fact a medical device?** Software whose intended purpose is regulatory data submission to EUDAMED would not obviously qualify under MDR Art. 2(1), which is the hook that pulls HWG in via § 1(1) no. 1a. You have told me it is a Class I device, and I have reviewed on that basis. But if the Class I self-certification does not actually cover this software, or covers a different module, then **UWG § 5(2) nos. 3 and 4 ("Status, Zulassung")** are engaged by any CE mark, class, or "medical device" designation appearing near this block — independently of whether the performance claims hold. Worth a five-minute check against the DoC before publishing.

**Gating.** You have specified Fachkreise, and I have applied that. If the block sits on an ungated public web page, the audience question reopens — a B2B page anyone can read is not automatically Fachkreise. For what it's worth, even on a Publikum reading, none of §  11(1) nos. 7, 8, 9, 11 or 12 bites on this particular copy: there is no health-impairment-by-non-use framing, no testimonial, no advertorial, no under-14 targeting. The audience question changes little here.

**Language.** Copy supplied in English for a German-market asset. Nothing in the provisions I verify requires German, but note the § 6(2) no. 2 verifiability test runs on what *this* audience can check — if you publish a German-language page, the linked benchmark methodology should be reachable in German too. Say the word and I'll give you the rewrite in German.

## Paste-ready rewrite

Placeholders in `[brackets]` are yours to fill; the structure is what carries the § 6(2) no. 2 compliance.

> **Every mandatory field checked before you submit.**
> Our EUDAMED module runs `[N]` automated checks against the current EUDAMED `[version]` schema, covering all mandatory Basic UDI-DI and UDI-DI fields, so format and completeness errors surface in the tool rather than on rejection.
> In our `[Month Year]` benchmark of `[N]` Class I submissions, median time from data entry to a complete submission was `[X]` minutes, against `[Y]` minutes for `[named comparator / unassisted manual entry]`. Full method: `[url]`.

What changed and why:

- "Competitors leave you guessing" → deleted. Replaced by a positive, checkable statement of what your tool does ("errors surface in the tool rather than on rejection"), which makes the same point without characterising anyone else's product.
- "every field" → "all mandatory ... fields" **plus** the named schema version. Narrow the claim to what you can actually evidence. If you do validate optional fields too, say so explicitly and keep the enumeration — the fix is precision, not hedging.
- "3x faster than the alternatives" → a stated metric, a stated comparator, a stated date, and a link to the method. Per the reference material's own risk logic: a claim that is verifiable and narrow is cheap to defend; a broad unverifiable claim is expensive **even when it is true**. If the benchmark won't support a specific comparator, drop the comparison and publish your own absolute figure.
- "legacy" → dropped. It carried no information and only added § 6(2) no. 5 exposure.

## Evidence to gather before publishing

| Claim | Evidence needed | From whom |
|---|---|---|
| Field-validation coverage | Field-by-field mapping of validation rules to the current EUDAMED schema; confirmation of mandatory vs. optional coverage, and syntax vs. content checks | Product / engineering |
| "3x faster" | Dated benchmark: defined task, comparator set, sample size, published methodology at a reachable URL | Product marketing + whoever ran it |
| Comparator scope | Confirmation that named/implied "alternatives" share the same Bedarf/Zweckbestimmung (§ 6(2) no. 1) | Regulatory / product |
| Intended purpose | The intended purpose verbatim from the technical documentation / DoC — unblocks limb (d) | Regulatory affairs |
| Device status | DoC and Class I self-certification scope — confirm it covers *this* software | Regulatory affairs |
| Likely risk | Whether the IFU / risk management file records over-reliance on automated validation as a risk | Regulatory affairs |

## Provisions cited

| Provision | Reference file | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| MDR Art. 7(a), (c), (d) | `references/mdr-ivdr-art7.md` | `[verified]` |
| HWG § 1(1) no. 1a, § 3 sentence 1, § 3 no. 1, § 11(1) nos. 7–9, 11, 12 | `references/hwg.md` | `[verified]` |
| UWG § 5(1), § 5(2) nos. 1, 3, 4 | `references/uwg.md` | `[verified]` |
| UWG § 6(1), § 6(2) nos. 1, 2, 5 | `references/uwg.md` | `[verified]` |

No `[verify]`-tier sources were relied on. I have not asserted how any German court would decide any of the above.

## Limits

> This review checks copy against the verbatim text of MDR Art. 7, IVDR Art. 7, HWG §§ 3 and 11, and UWG §§ 5 and 6, retrieved from EUR-Lex and gesetze-im-internet on 2026-09-09. It does **not** cover case law, MDCG guidance, notified-body practice, national enforcement decisions, or any market outside the EU and Germany. UWG in particular is heavily shaped by BGH and OLG case law that this review does not assess. It is a drafting and risk-triage aid, not legal advice, and it is not a substitute for a Fachanwalt für Medizinrecht or Wettbewerbsrecht.

---

**The one thing to take away:** the "3x faster" claim is not primarily a truth problem — it is a verifiability problem, and publishing a *true* 3x figure without a reachable methodology leaves § 6(2) no. 2 exposure intact. Since UWG arrives as an Abmahnung from a competitor rather than a regulator's letter, the party most motivated to test that sentence is the "legacy tool" vendor you've just made erkennbar.

If you paste the intended purpose from the DoC, I'll run the limb (d) pass on the rewritten block.

graders.evidence:
Both reference layers read. Two scoping points before the findings, since they change which law applies.

**Anchor 1 — intended purpose: not supplied.** I can review limbs (a), (b) and (c) without it, but MDR Art. 7(d) — suggesting uses beyond the assessed intended purpose — is the limb device marketing trips most often, and I can't assess it against a purpose I haven't seen. Can you paste the intended purpose from the technical documentation or DoC?

**Anchor 2 — audience: Fachkreise, on your statement.** Manufacturers and regulatory consultants are squarely Fachkreise, so **HWG § 11 does not apply** and I raise nothing under it. One check: if this block sits on an ungated public web page, the Fachkreise characterisation is worth a second look — § 11 nos. 7, 8, 9, 11, 12 would come into scope. § 3 applies either way.

**A third point that changes the analysis.** The copy markets a EUDAMED submission tool, but you've described the product as a Class I software device. Those don't obviously coincide — a regulatory-submission utility usually has no medical purpose under MDR Art. 2(1). Either (i) the submission tool *is* the Class I device, and MDR Art. 7 + HWG both apply as below; (ii) the submission tool is a separate, non-device product, in which case **only UWG applies** and every MDR/HWG citation below drops away; or (iii) it's a module of a larger device. My findings hold under (i) and (iii). Under (ii), the UWG § 6 findings — which are the substantive ones here — survive unchanged. Worth confirming which.

# Device Claims Review: comparison block

**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09
**Device:** EUDAMED submission software — Class I (per user); no notified body implied by copy
**Intended purpose (as assessed):** NOT SUPPLIED — limb (d) not assessed
**Audience:** Fachkreise (manufacturers, regulatory consultants) — § 11 not applied; confirm page is gated
**Markets:** DE (EU layer also engaged)

## Summary

3 claims reviewed. **1 cut, 2 reword/substantiate, 0 OK.**

The whole block is comparative advertising under UWG § 6(1) — "legacy EUDAMED tools" makes competitors *erkennbar* even though none is named (`uwg.md` uses this near-exact phrase as its illustration). Comparison is lawful in Germany; it just has to clear § 6(2) cumulatively. The recurring failure here is § 6(2) no. 2 **nachprüfbar** — a reader cannot check any of the three assertions from public information. That is also the expensive failure mode: broad and unverifiable is costly to defend even when true.

**Ready to publish:** No — rewrite needed. All three sentences need change.

## Findings

---

**Claim:** "Competitors leave you guessing."
**Breach:** UWG § 6(2) no. 2
**Why:** A blanket negative about all competitors, tied to no *wesentliche, relevante, nachprüfbare und typische Eigenschaft* — there is no characteristic stated, so there is nothing objective for the reader to verify.
**Evidence needed:** n/a — cannot be cured by evidence. There is no proposition here to substantiate.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 6(2) no. 5 (*herabsetzt oder verunglimpft*) — an undifferentiated disparagement of the entire competitive field. Whether this crosses into denigration is shaped by case law this review does not assess `[verify]`.
**Call:** Cut

---

**Claim:** "3x faster than the alternatives."
**Breach:** UWG § 6(2) no. 2
**Why:** Faster at what task, against which alternatives, measured how? None is stated, so the figure is not *nachprüfbar* from public information and is not anchored to a specified characteristic. This fails no. 2 even if the number is accurate.
**Evidence needed:** The benchmark itself — task definition, comparator set named or characterised, sample, method, date — and a public pointer the reader can reach.
**Also engaged:**
- UWG § 5(2) no. 1 — *von der Verwendung zu erwartende Ergebnisse* and *Tests*, if the underlying benchmark is unrepresentative or cherry-picked. Note that no. 1 covers the *wesentliche Bestandteile* of tests, so a real benchmark presented without its material conditions is still in scope.
- HWG § 3 (general *Irreführung*), esp. no. 3(a) *Beschaffenheit* — if the figure does not hold for typical use.
- MDR Art. 7(a) — if throughput is a claimed performance characteristic of the device and the figure is unsupported. Its primary home is UWG, but Art. 7 reaches text misleading "with regard to the device's ... performance".

**Call:** Needs substantiation + rewording

---

**Claim:** "Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools, we validate every field before submission."
**Breach:** UWG § 6(2) no. 2
**Why:** Two problems, one provision. The comparator class "legacy EUDAMED tools" is undefined, so the reader cannot identify the set being compared — and the implied negative (that those tools do *not* validate) is therefore uncheckable. *Nachprüfbarkeit* fails on the comparison, independently of whether your own half is true.
**Evidence needed:** For the comparison: a defined comparator set and a dated, checkable basis for the negative. For your own half: confirmation that validation genuinely covers **every** field of the submission types you support — "every" is absolute and a single conditional or unvalidated field falsifies it.
**Also engaged:**
- UWG § 5(2) no. 1 — *wesentliche Merkmale*, *Zwecktauglichkeit*, if "every field" overstates coverage.
- MDR Art. 7(a) — ascribing a property the device does not have, on the same condition.
- MDR Art. 7(d) — **cannot be assessed.** If the assessed intended purpose is narrower than the copy implies (e.g. covers only certain EUDAMED modules, actor registration only, or specific device classes), "every field before submission" suggests use beyond it. This is the cure-path distinction that matters: (a) is fixed by evidence, (d) is not — it is fixed by narrowing the claim or extending the conformity assessment.
- **§ 6 scoping nuance:** to the extent "legacy EUDAMED tools" is read as the Commission's own EUDAMED interface and XML bulk-upload facility, that is not a *Mitbewerber*, so § 6 does not reach that part of the comparison — but § 5 still does.

**Call:** Needs rewording + substantiation

---

**MDR Art. 7(c) — open question, not a finding.** The copy is benefit-only and surfaces no limitation. I can't tell from what I have whether the IFU records a likely risk that belongs here — the obvious candidate for a validation tool is that passing validation is not a guarantee of regulatory acceptance, but I'm not going to flag (c) on a risk I inferred from the product category rather than read in your material. Worth checking against the IFU. If the IFU does record something in that shape, note that a residual-risk statement here would also head off HWG § 3 no. 2(a) *Erfolg mit Sicherheit* — "validate every field before submission" sits close to an implied guarantee of clean submission, and § 3 no. 2(a) has no MDR Art. 7 equivalent.

**Not raised, deliberately:** the copy makes no claim about class, CE status, notified-body involvement or certificate scope, so UWG § 5(2) nos. 3 and 4 are not engaged. HWG § 3a applies to *Arzneimittel* only.

## Suggested fix — paste-ready

Two versions. Bracketed values are yours to fill; the structure is what does the compliance work.

**A — keeps the comparison (higher effort, higher payoff):**

> Every mandatory field is validated against the EUDAMED [module, e.g. Actor/Device registration] data dictionary [version] before you submit, with errors flagged in-app. In [month/year] internal benchmarking, preparing [N] Class [X] registrations took [A] minutes with [product] versus [B] minutes using [named comparator or defined class, e.g. "manual entry in the EUDAMED web interface"] — method and dataset: [link].

**B — drops the comparison (lower risk, publish today):**

> Every mandatory field is validated against the EUDAMED [module] data dictionary [version] before you submit, with errors flagged in-app — so format and completeness errors surface in your workflow, not after submission.

Three drafting notes: name or define the comparator rather than gesturing at "legacy tools"; make the benchmark reachable by link, since § 6(2) no. 2 turns on the reader being able to check; and if validation does not in fact cover literally every field, replace "every mandatory field" with the true scope — the narrow claim is cheap to defend, the absolute one is not.

## Evidence to gather before publishing

| Claim | Evidence needed | From whom |
|---|---|---|
| "3x faster" | Benchmark protocol, comparator set, sample, date, publishable summary | Product / marketing ops |
| "validate every field" | Field-coverage matrix per supported submission type; confirmation no field is unvalidated | Engineering / product |
| "legacy EUDAMED tools" (negative) | Defined comparator set + dated basis for the negative, or delete the comparison | Marketing + competitive intel |
| Intended purpose | Verbatim text from technical documentation / DoC — needed for limb (d) | Regulatory affairs |
| Likely risk | Whether the IFU records a likely risk (e.g. validation ≠ acceptance) | Regulatory affairs |
| Page gating | Whether the block sits behind Fachkreise gating | Web / marketing |

## Provisions cited

- MDR Art. 7(a), (c), (d) — `references/mdr-ivdr-art7.md` `[verified]`
- HWG § 1(1) no. 1a, § 3, § 3 no. 2(a), § 3 no. 3(a) — `references/hwg.md` `[verified]`
- HWG § 11 — `references/hwg.md` `[verified]` — **not applied**, audience is Fachkreise
- UWG § 5(1), § 5(2) no. 1 — `references/uwg.md` `[verified]`
- UWG § 6(1), § 6(2) nos. 1, 2, 5 — `references/uwg.md` `[verified]`
- Denigration threshold under § 6(2) no. 5 `[verify]` — case-law-dependent, not verified here

## Limits

> This review checks copy against the verbatim text of MDR Art. 7, IVDR Art. 7, HWG §§ 3 and 11, and UWG §§ 5 and 6, retrieved from EUR-Lex and gesetze-im-internet on 2026-09-09. It does **not** cover case law, MDCG guidance, notified-body practice, national enforcement decisions, or any market outside the EU and Germany. UWG in particular is heavily shaped by BGH and OLG case law that this review does not assess. It is a drafting and risk-triage aid, not legal advice, and it is not a substitute for a Fachanwalt für Medizinrecht or Wettbewerbsrecht.

---

Two things back to you: the **intended purpose** text, so I can run limb (d) on "validate every field" — and confirmation of **whether the marketed submission tool is the Class I device itself**, since under reading (ii) above the MDR and HWG layers drop out entirely and this becomes a pure UWG § 6 review.

graders.evidence:
## Verdict

All three sentences carry real risk. The strongest exposure is not MDR — it's German competition law. This copy is close to a textbook `§ 6 UWG` comparative-advertising problem and would be an easy target for a competitor *Abmahnung* (cease-and-desist with cost reimbursement and a penalty-backed undertaking), which in practice is faster and more painful than any regulator action.

## Findings

**1. "3x faster than the alternatives" — unverifiable superiority claim (highest risk)**

`§ 6(2) Nr. 2 UWG` requires comparisons to be objective and *verifiable* (*nachprüfbar*) on relevant, typical features. "The alternatives" names no reference group, no metric, no conditions. A reader cannot check it, which is precisely what the provision forbids — independent of whether the number is true. Add `§ 5 UWG` (misleading) and, if the product is genuinely a device, `§ 3 HWG` (attributing performance the product does not have).

Fix requires all of: what is measured (time to complete a submission? data-entry time? validation runtime?), against what named or clearly delimited comparator, under what method, with what sample size and date. You must hold the substantiation at the moment of publication — assembling it after an *Abmahnung* lands is too late.

**2. "Competitors leave you guessing" — disparagement**

`§ 4 Nr. 1` and `§ 6(2) Nr. 5 UWG` prohibit *Herabsetzung/Verunglimpfung*. This is a blanket negative assertion about every competitor's product quality with zero factual anchor. There is no substantiation route for it — it has to go. Say what your product does; don't characterise what theirs fails to do.

**3. "legacy EUDAMED tools" — disparaging and factually fragile**

Two problems. It's a pejorative sweep across unnamed competitors (same provisions as above). And EUDAMED's mandatory phase-in is recent enough that a "legacy tool" cohort is hard to evidence at all — a court or opponent will ask which products you mean and since when. Weak claims that can't be pinned down are the ones that lose.

**4. "we validate every field before submission" — absolute claim, most likely false as written**

"Every field" is a falsifiable absolute. It breaks if there is any conditional field, free-text field, cross-record consistency rule, or server-side EUDAMED rule your tool doesn't cover. One counterexample makes it misleading under `§ 5 UWG`.

There's a second layer: the copy invites users to infer the tool guarantees an accepted, compliant submission. Regulatory accountability stays with the manufacturer or authorised representative. That implied reliance is the part most likely to generate a real complaint from a customer whose submission was rejected.

**5. Don't imply Commission affiliation**

"EUDAMED" is a Commission-operated system. Referential use is fine, but the layout must not suggest endorsement, certification, or official partnership (`§ 5(1) Nr. 3 UWG` — misleading as to affiliation). For a Class I self-certified product, also avoid anything implying notified-body or authority approval.

**6. Two things you do *not* need**

No *Pflichttext* — `§ 4 HWG` mandatory-particulars rules apply to medicinal products, not devices. And English-language B2B copy aimed at *Fachkreise* is generally acceptable; the German-language obligation attaches to labelling and IFU under the MPDG, not to advertising. Don't over-comply here.

## Scoping question that changes the analysis

A tool that validates EUDAMED registration data for manufacturers has no medical purpose and would not normally be a medical device at all. If it is nonetheless being placed on the market as Class I with a CE mark, that's a separate and more serious issue than the copy — and it means MDR Art. 7 plus every claim must trace to the declared intended purpose and to verification records in the technical documentation. If it is *not* a device, MDR Art. 7 and HWG drop out and you are governed by UWG alone.

The review below assumes the device framing you gave me. Findings 1–5 hold either way; only the MDR/HWG citations depend on the answer.

## Suggested rewrite

> Field-level validation against the current EUDAMED data dictionary. Required and conditional fields are checked as you enter them, so format and completeness errors surface before you submit rather than after rejection.
>
> In internal testing on [n] Basic UDI-DI registrations (method and date: [x]), teams completed data entry [n]% faster than with a manual spreadsheet-to-portal workflow. Method available on request.
>
> Responsibility for the accuracy and completeness of registration data remains with the manufacturer or authorised representative.

What changed: the superiority claim is scoped to a named comparator with a stated method; "every field" becomes the specific, defensible "required and conditional fields"; both competitor jabs are gone; the reliance disclaimer is explicit.

If you want to keep the comparative punch, the compliant shape is a named-competitor comparison on one measurable feature with published methodology — that is permitted under `§ 6 UWG` and is far safer than a vague sweep, though it raises the substantiation bar considerably.

## Before publishing

Keep a claims dossier holding, per claim: the exact wording, the metric and method, the raw data, the comparator products and their versions and test dates, sign-off, and publication date. Re-verify on every EUDAMED schema change — a "3x faster" or "validates every field" claim that was true against last year's dictionary goes stale silently, and staleness is a `§ 5 UWG` exposure of its own. If the device framing is correct, the validation function and any performance claim should also be reflected in the intended purpose and V&V records, not live only in marketing.

graders.evidence:
## Threshold issue: is this actually a Class I device?

The brief says Class I software device, but the copy describes a EUDAMED submission tool — validating registration fields for manufacturers. That has no medical purpose under MDR Art. 2(1), so it would normally fall outside the MDR entirely. This matters because it decides which rulebook applies:

- **If it is a Class I device:** MDR Art. 7 and the Heilmittelwerbegesetz (§ 3 HWG, misleading advertising for Medizinprodukte) bite, and every performance claim must be consistent with the intended purpose in your technical documentation and supported by your clinical evaluation.
- **If it is regulatory tooling, not a device:** only UWG applies — but then "Class I" must never appear in your own marketing, because self-describing as a regulated device you aren't is itself misleading under § 5 UWG.

Resolve this before the copy ships. Everything below assumes the MDR case and flags where it differs.

## Findings

**1. "Competitors leave you guessing" — disparagement, § 6(2) Nr. 5 UWG**

This is the highest-risk line. Comparative advertising is lawful in Germany, but § 6(2) Nr. 5 prohibits *Herabsetzung* — discrediting a competitor's goods or business. A bare assertion that competitors leave customers "guessing," with no objective feature behind it, is characterisation rather than comparison. In a market as narrow as EUDAMED tooling, competitors are identifiable without being named, which is enough to trigger § 6. Germany's *Abmahnung* practice means the realistic downside is a competitor cease-and-desist with cost recovery and a penalty-backed undertaking, not a regulator. Cut the line.

**2. "3x faster than the alternatives" — unsubstantiated superiority claim**

This reads as *Spitzenstellungswerbung*. German courts expect the advertiser to hold substantiation at the time of publication, and in practice you carry the evidentiary burden if challenged. As written it fails on three counts: no metric (faster at what — field entry, review cycle, time to accepted submission?), no comparator set ("the alternatives" is undefined), and no measurement basis. Either footnote a defined benchmark or drop the multiple.

**3. "validate every field" — absolute claim**

"Every" is falsifiable by a single unvalidated field, and it conflates syntactic validation against the EUDAMED schema with substantive regulatory correctness. Under MDR Art. 7(a) this risks ascribing a property the device does not have; it also invites reliance that shifts perceived liability onto you when a submission is rejected. Bound it: which fields, against what ruleset.

**4. "Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools" — comparison on a non-objective axis**

§ 6(2) Nr. 2 requires comparison of objectively verifiable, relevant, typical features. "Legacy" is a pejorative framing, not a feature. Compare capability, or compare nothing.

**5. Secondary points**

- Don't pair "EUDAMED" with EU insignia or wording implying Commission endorsement.
- If any accompanying copy states EUDAMED module mandatory dates, verify each against the current Official Journal position — module obligations have been phased, and a stale deadline is a § 5 UWG misleading statement in its own right.
- Professional audience means § 11 HWG (lay advertising) is largely out of scope, but a public website is accessible to laypersons; gate the material behind a professional context if you rely on that.
- Marketing copy isn't labelling, so the German-language requirement under § 8 MPDG doesn't strictly apply — but English-only promotional material for a German buyer is a commercial liability regardless.

## Suggested rewrite

> **Every mandatory EUDAMED field checked before you submit.**
> [N] automated checks run against the current EUDAMED data exchange schema, flagging incomplete and inconsistent entries at entry rather than at rejection.
>
> In internal testing (Q[X] 2026, n = [X] device registrations), teams completed Actor and UDI/Device registration in one third of the time required by their previous spreadsheet-based workflow.¹
>
> ¹ Comparator, dataset and measurement method: [link]

This keeps the substance — pre-submission validation, a real speed advantage — while moving the comparison onto your own prior-workflow baseline, which you can actually evidence, and removing the competitor characterisation entirely.

## Substantiation to hold on file before publication

1. Benchmark protocol for the speed claim: comparator identity, task definition, sample size, date, who ran it. Dated and retained.
2. The exact field list your validation covers, mapped to the EUDAMED schema version, with a change process for when the schema updates.
3. If Class I: confirmation that "validates every mandatory field" sits inside the intended purpose in your technical documentation, and that the claim is traceable to clinical evaluation output as required under MDR Art. 7 and Annex XIV.
4. A screenshot-dated copy of the published claim, so you can show what was substantiated when.

The one item I'd treat as blocking is finding 1 — the disparagement line is the kind of thing that draws a competitor *Abmahnung* on its own, independent of whether the speed claim holds up.

graders.evidence:
## Verdict

Three sentences, three separate exposure points. As written I'd hold this copy — the middle sentence is the one most likely to draw an *Abmahnung*, and the first sentence is the one most likely to be a factual misstatement about your own product. (Regulatory/competition read, not legal advice; have counsel clear the final wording.)

---

## Clause-by-clause

**1. "Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools…" — comparative advertising, medium-high risk**

You don't have to name a competitor for § 6 UWG to bite; the comparison only has to make competitors *identifiable*. The EUDAMED tooling market is small enough that "legacy EUDAMED tools" points at a recognizable handful of vendors. Once § 6 applies, the comparison must be objective, and rest on features that are material, relevant, verifiable and representative (§ 6 Abs. 2 Nr. 2 UWG). "Legacy" is a pejorative characterization, not a verifiable feature.

*Fix:* either drop the comparative frame and make a positive claim about your own behavior, or compare on a named, measurable dimension.

**2. "Competitors leave you guessing." — highest risk, remove**

This is blanket denigration with no factual anchor — § 6 Abs. 2 Nr. 5 UWG (Herabsetzung/Verunglimpfung), and § 4 Nr. 1 UWG independently. There is no substantiation path for it, because it isn't a claim about a measurable property; it's an unflattering generalization. It is also the sentence that gets worse in translation: a natural German rendering ("Andere lassen Sie im Dunkeln") reads harsher than the English.

*Fix:* delete. Replace with what your product does, stated affirmatively.

**3. "3x faster than the alternatives." — high risk, unsubstantiable as written**

Problems stack:
- **Faster at what?** No metric. Submission preparation time? Validation runtime? Records per hour? An unspecified performance dimension is not verifiable, so it fails § 6 Abs. 2 Nr. 2 UWG on its face.
- **Than which alternatives?** "The alternatives" implies the whole market, including tools you almost certainly haven't benchmarked.
- **Burden of proof is yours.** In German practice the advertiser carries the burden for the accuracy of a comparative claim, and for a superiority claim must show the lead is substantial *and* durable ("Vorsprung von einiger Dauer") — a one-off benchmark that a competitor's next release erodes won't hold.
- **If you cite a study or benchmark report**, § 6 HWG requires you to name the author, the date, and the source in the advertising itself.

*Fix:* narrow to one named metric, one named comparison set, with a dated methodology footnote — and diary a re-validation cadence.

**4. "we validate every field before submission" — misleading-absolute, medium-high risk**

This is a claim about your own product, so § 5 UWG (and § 3 HWG if the device framing holds). "Every field" is only true if you validate every field of every EUDAMED module — Actor, UDI/Device, Certificate, Vigilance, Clinical Investigation, Market Surveillance — including conditional and free-text fields, against the current DTX schema. It also invites the reading that validation is *semantic*, not just format/schema conformance, and therefore that passing your check predicts acceptance.

*Fix:* scope it to the modules and schema version you actually cover, and state expressly that validation does not replace the manufacturer's own data verification (the obligation stays with them under MDR Art. 10 / Art. 31).

**5. MDR Art. 7 — applies if the device framing is correct**

Art. 7 prohibits text, signs or claims that mislead as to intended purpose, safety and performance. "3x faster" is a performance claim: it must sit inside the declared intended purpose and be supported by data in your technical documentation. For a Class I self-declaration this is exactly the kind of marketing/TD mismatch an authority spot-check finds. Also ensure nothing in the copy implies notified-body involvement.

---

## One structural flag

You describe this as a **Class I software device**, but the product as described — validating registration fields before EUDAMED submission — has no medical purpose under MDR Art. 2(1) and wouldn't qualify under Rule 11. Either:

- the EUDAMED tool is **not** the device, and marketing copy is blending two products (fix: separate the claims completely — device claims must not attach to the RA tooling); or
- it is genuinely being CE-marked as Class I, in which case the classification rationale needs a hard look, because CE-marking a non-device and advertising it as one is its own problem under MDR Art. 20 and § 5 UWG.

Worth resolving before the copy question, since it changes which rulebook governs the whole page.

---

## Suggested rewrite

**EN**

> Every mandatory field is checked against the current EUDAMED DTX schema (v[X.Y]) before you submit — Actor and UDI/Device modules — so schema errors surface in your workspace, not in a rejected upload.
>
> In our [Month YYYY] benchmark, preparing a 500-device UDI-DI batch took [N] minutes with [Product] versus [M] minutes using [named comparator / manual spreadsheet-and-upload workflow] — a [2.9]× reduction in preparation time. Methodology: [link].
>
> Validation supports, and does not replace, the manufacturer's verification of registration data under MDR Art. 10 and Art. 31.

**DE**

> Alle Pflichtfelder werden vor der Übermittlung gegen das aktuelle EUDAMED-DTX-Schema (v[X.Y]) geprüft — Module „Actor" und „UDI/Device". Schemafehler werden so bereits im Arbeitsbereich sichtbar, nicht erst beim abgelehnten Upload.
>
> In unserem Benchmark vom [Monat JJJJ] betrug die Vorbereitungszeit für eine Charge von 500 UDI-DI mit [Produkt] [N] Minuten gegenüber [M] Minuten mit [benannter Vergleichslösung] — eine Verkürzung um den Faktor [2,9]. Methodik: [Link]. Quelle: [Autor], [Datum].
>
> Die Prüfung unterstützt die Verifizierung der Registrierungsdaten durch den Hersteller gemäß Art. 10 und Art. 31 MDR, ersetzt sie jedoch nicht.

Note the rewrite drops the comparative *frame* but keeps a comparative *claim* — that's deliberate. A specific, sourced, dated comparison is defensible under § 6 UWG; a vague pejorative one isn't.

---

## Substantiation file to assemble before publishing

| Claim | Evidence needed |
|---|---|
| Field validation coverage | Field-by-field coverage matrix per module, mapped to DTX schema version; change-control tie to schema updates |
| Speed factor | Written protocol, dataset, hardware/network conditions, operator skill level, run dates, raw timings, comparator version and licence provenance |
| Durability of the speed lead | Re-benchmark schedule (quarterly is defensible) + trigger on comparator major releases |
| Performance claim vs. TD | Cross-reference to intended purpose and performance data in technical documentation (MDR Art. 7) |
| Any cited study | Author, date, publication reference printed in the ad (§ 6 HWG) |

Also worth checking: German is the operative market language here, so the German copy — not the English — is what a court would assess, and the claims should be reviewed in that version rather than translated after sign-off.
